requirement_text.REQ-067: Port src/api/pagination.zig (406 lines, R-Co's API-06) as Letflow.Api.Pagination -- the shared cursor encode/decode, prefix validation, expiry checking, page-size validation, and standardised page response that every S4 list endpoint delegates to. SECURITY (INV-1, INV-5): the decoded cursor struct must have no tenant/schema field -- tenant scoping comes exclusively from REQ-072's future resolved request context, never from the cursor. A cursor minted in tenant A and replayed against tenant B must return tenant B's page or an error, never tenant A's rows.

task.description:
Security gate on `lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex`, commit `0514174` on `feature/WF02-REQ067-20260821`, per `docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md`. This module is explicitly named in REQ-067 as INV-1/INV-5 relevant, so this is in scope -- do not PASS it out-of-scope without reading the actual code first.

1. Read `git diff main...HEAD` (or the file directly, since it's new) and confirm this diff touches a tenant-data-adjacent path per the security-invariants doc's applicability notes -- state the scope test's result explicitly either way.
2. For each of INV-1..INV-8, determine APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE against this diff and state which.
3. For INV-1 specifically (per-tenant isolation): read the actual `Cursor` struct definition in `lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex` yourself. Confirm it has exactly the fields the design specified and NONE of them is a tenant id, schema name, or any value that could widen a query's scope. This is the load-bearing check for this entire gate.
4. Confirm nothing in this module reads or writes `Letflow.Repo`, issues SQL, or touches any tenant-scoped table (the design claims this module is pure/stateless -- verify by reading the actual file, not by trusting the claim).
5. Confirm `decode_cursor/4`'s caller-supplied `prefix`/`expiry_ts_offset`/`expiry_window_us` parameters cannot themselves be used to bypass a check (e.g. could a caller pass an empty prefix or a huge offset to defeat validation?) -- if you find a real gap, this is a FAIL naming the specific bypass; if you conclude it is not exploitable (e.g. because these parameters are supplied by the ENDPOINT code, not by the external caller, and the external caller only supplies the encoded cursor string), state that reasoning explicitly.
6. For each APPLIES invariant, run its 'How to verify' check per the security-invariants doc.
7. FAIL immediately on any applicable invariant failing -- all BLOCKER, no partial credit, per WF-02 Step 2c's own procedure.

Complete your work synchronously within this turn per `core-directives.md`'s rule.
acceptance_criteria: The scope test result is stated explicitly, and given REQ-067's own INV-1/INV-5 framing, this is confirmed in scope rather than dismissed
Each of INV-1..INV-8 is stated as APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE against this specific diff
The Cursor struct's field set is read directly from the actual .ex file and confirmed to contain no tenant/schema/scope-widening field
This module is confirmed to contain no Repo/SQL/tenant-table access, verified by reading the file rather than trusting the design's claim
The caller-supplied-parameter bypass question (prefix/offset/window) is reasoned through explicitly, with a concrete answer -- not left implicit
A PASS/FAIL verdict is recorded per WF-02 Step 2c's own procedure, with every APPLIES invariant's verification check actually run

result.summary: Scope test: IN SCOPE. REQ-067 explicitly frames lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex as INV-1/INV-5 relevant (cursor must carry no tenant/schema field), and it is response-shaping/data-access-path building-block code every future S4 list endpoint will delegate to -- reviewed accordingly rather than dismissed as 'not yet a tenant-data path'. Per-invariant verdicts: INV-1 APPLIES (per REQ-067's explicit framing and the applicability note's 'checkable on any diff touching a tenant-scoped table, schema, or migration' -- this diff touches none of those literally, since the module has no Ecto schema/migration/Repo call, but REQ-067 dispatches it as the structural guarantee future schema-scoped queries will rely on, so verified anyway) -- PASS: read Cursor struct directly (pagination.ex:43-57), `defstruct [:inner]`, @type t :: %__MODULE__{inner: binary()} -- exactly one field, no tenant_id/schema/prefix/scope field of any kind, matching the design's §0.3/§2.1 spec exactly. INV-1's literal (a)/(b)/(c) Repo-prefix checklist does not apply (no Repo call exists in this module) -- noted explicitly rather than force-fit. INV-2 NOT-APPLICABLE: no concrete API response type/route handler ships in this requirement (design §9's explicit scope boundary: 'does not ship any concrete list endpoint'); Page's field selection (items/next_cursor/count) is not tenant-data field authorization, it's a generic envelope. INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE (S5, unrelated). INV-4 NOT-APPLICABLE: no secret/env/config resolution touched by this diff (grep for System.get_env/secret patterns confirmed nothing added). INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE: no concrete lookup-by-ID endpoint ships here (same §9 scope boundary) -- though noted the module's error atoms (:wrong_endpoint/:invalid_cursor/:expired/:invalid_base64) are already endpoint-agnostic and carry no tenant-existence signal, which will help whichever future endpoint implements INV-5's indistinguishability requirement. INV-6 APPLIES and is satisfied by this review itself existing with an explicit per-invariant statement (the meta-invariant's own definition of satisfaction). INV-7 NOT-APPLICABLE to this diff: grepped `Repo.query` repo-wide -- all 7 hits are in pre-existing files (sandbox_pool.ex, sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex, tenant_provisioning.ex), none in pagination.ex, none added by this diff; also confirmed via direct read that pagination.ex contains no Repo/Ecto/Plug.Conn reference at all. INV-8 APPLIES (cursor/page-size values are caller-controlled, network-facing input) -- PASS: read every function in the file; every fallible path (url_decode, check_prefix, extract_expiry_timestamp, check_expiry, parse_page_size_param, validate_page_size, parse_int_from_cursor) returns a tagged tuple, no bare pattern match that can raise on malformed input; grep for bare `{:ok, ...} =` found only a safe `case`-clause match on an already-destructured tuple (line 241), not a raise-capable bare match. Check-5 bypass reasoning: `decode_cursor/4`'s 2nd-4th args (prefix, expiry_ts_offset, expiry_window_us) are NOT external-caller-controlled -- the module has zero Plug.Conn/query-param access (confirmed by direct read), so nothing in this diff derives them from request input; per the design (§0.1/§5), the intended call-site convention is that each future endpoint passes its own hardcoded per-endpoint literal (e.g. "T:" for tasks) for prefix/offset, while only `encoded` (the opaque cursor string) originates from the HTTP client. Concretely: an external caller supplying an empty or malicious `encoded` string cannot force wrong_endpoint/expiry bypass, because those checks run against whatever prefix/offset THIS module's caller (not the HTTP client) supplied. I did trace one real internal risk for completeness: if some future endpoint's own code mistakenly called decode_cursor/4 with prefix="" (0 bytes), check_prefix/2's `byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix)` guard would trivially pass for any decoded value, defeating cross-endpoint isolation -- but this is a hypothetical misuse by a not-yet-written caller, not a defect in this module or an external-caller-reachable bypass in the code that exists today; flagged as guidance for future ELIXIR-DEV work (REQ-072/route-handler requirements) rather than a FAIL here, since no such caller exists yet to actually exhibit it (design §9 scope boundary). No FAIL found on any APPLIES invariant. Verdict: PASS.

issues.description: Guidance for future S4 route-handler work (REQ-072 onward, not this requirement): decode_cursor/4's prefix argument must always be a hardcoded per-endpoint literal supplied by the route handler, never derived from any request-controlled value (query param, header, path segment). A caller passing an empty or attacker-influenced prefix would defeat the cross-endpoint isolation check_prefix/2 provides (byte_size(decoded) >= byte_size(prefix) trivially holds for a 0-byte prefix). No such caller exists yet -- pagination.ex ships no concrete endpoint (design §9) -- so this is not a defect in the current diff, just a note for whichever future ELIXIR-DEV handoff wires the first real decode_cursor/4 call site.
